title: TLS/SRTP configuration (FreePBX + Polycom + Yealink + Stretto softphone)
body:
Org policy: engage a Hosted Engineer before implementing. Only fully tested on Yealink models — treat Polycom/Stretto as less proven.

FreePBX side: Admin > Certificate Manager — generate (or reuse) a Let's Encrypt certificate and set it as Default; the built-in default cert can't be used for this. Settings > Asterisk SIP Settings > SIP Settings [chan_pjsip] tab: in TLS/SSL/SRTP Settings, pick that Let's Encrypt cert in Certificate Manager, SSL Method = tlsv1_2, Verify Client = No, Verify Server = Yes. In Transports, set tls - 0.0.0.0 - All = Yes, and confirm the 0.0.0.0 (tls) port is 5061. On the General SIP Settings tab, set Allow Anonymous Inbound SIP Calls and Allow SIP Guests both to No. Restart Asterisk (fwconsole stop, fwconsole start). Per extension needing TLS, on the Advanced tab: Transport = Auto or 0.0.0.0-tls, Media Encryption = SRTP via in-SDP (recommended), Allow Non-Encrypted Media (Opportunistic SRTP) = No, Direct Media = No, DTLS disabled.

Polycom endpoint attributes (replace DOMAIN_OF_CUSTOMER_PBX with the actual PBX FQDN, e.g. pbxtest.123.net):
  device.sec.TLS.prov.strictCertCommonNameValidation=0
  device.sec.TLS.prov.strictCertCommonNameValidation.set=1
  sec.srtp.offer=1
  voIpProt.server.1.address=DOMAIN_OF_CUSTOMER_PBX
  voIpProt.server.1.port=5061
  voIpProt.server.1.transport=TLS
  reg.1.server.1.address=DOMAIN_OF_CUSTOMER_PBX
  reg.1.server.1.port=5061
  reg.1.server.1.transport=TLS
  reg.1.srtp.enable=1
  reg.1.srtp.offer=1

Yealink endpoint attributes:
  account.1.sip_server.1.address=DOMAIN_OF_CUSTOMER_PBX
  account.1.sip_server.1.port=5061
  account.1.sip_server.1.transport_type=2
  account.1.srtp_encryption=2
  security.default_ssl_method=3
  static.security.dev_cert=1
  static.security.trust_certificates=0

123NET Softphone (Stretto) — set per-User/Extension, or in sip.only to apply to all:
  account1Sip.domain = customer PBX domain
  account1Sip.ignoreTlsCertVerify = False
  account1Sip.proxy = customer PBX domain
  desk.network.transport.encryptAudioOption = True
  desk.network.transport.option = 2
  mob.network.siptransport.encryptAudio = 1
  mob.network.siptransport.option = 2

If TLS registration is failing after this, the certificate itself (expired/wrong CN/not set as Default) is the most common cause — check with the Certificate Status tool before re-checking every endpoint attribute.

title: ALGO 8301 paging adapter provisioning
body:
Standard 123.Net ALGO 8301 paging adapter setup:
1. Default web login: admin / algo.
2. Upgrade firmware from the GUI (auto-check/download — no progress bar, just a ~20 minute countdown). Note: auto-update sometimes fails from very old firmware (seen on v3.3.3) — if so, manually load an intermediate firmware file first (v3.4.4), then auto-update should proceed normally to the latest (e.g. v4.1.1).
3. Basic Settings > SIP: enter the PBX IP as SIP Domain/Proxy Server, and the paging extension's number/Authentication ID/password. Leave Ring/Alert Mode = None unless a specific ring-monitor behavior is wanted. The device auto-answers inbound calls to this extension and pages out audio (and multicast if configured).
4. Advanced Settings > Provisioning: set Provisioning Mode = Disabled, otherwise settings get wiped on reboot.
5. Basic Settings > Multicast: set Multicast Mode = Transmitter (Sender) for a standard single-zone overhead paging setup; pick Zone Selection Mode (DTMF Selectable vs Single Zone) and Multicast Type (Regular RTP is compatible with the widest range of endpoints).
6. Advanced Settings > Time: set the correct time zone.
7. Change the admin password from the default (standard fleet default: 08520852).
8. System > Maintenance: download the config and attach it to the asset record for tracking.

title: Ring Group
body: Ring Groups are groups of dialing-enabled entities (Extensions, other Ring Groups, Queues, phone numbers, etc.) that ring together when the Ring Group number is dialed. A Ring Group is assigned a number just like an extension. Settings (strategy, ring time, no-answer destination) control how it behaves.

title: Queue
body: Call Queues are similar to Ring Groups but offer more features. Callers are placed on hold in a virtual queue until an agent is available, hearing hold music/announcements/ringing per configuration. Queues can relay approximate hold time and position, and support a breakout IVR. Often used in call centers with limited staff handling high call volume.

title: IVR (Interactive Voice Response / Auto Attendant)
body: An IVR gathers caller input via keypad or voice response and routes the call based on the option selected — to an extension, ring group, or other destination. Also known as an Auto Attendant.

title: ATA (Analog Telephone Adapter)
body: An ATA bridges an analog device (phone or fax machine) onto the SIP/PBX network, registering as a normal extension. Common models: Grandstream HT802, Cisco/Linksys SPA122. A DID routed to an extension whose registered device is an ATA with a physical fax machine attached is a very common real-world fax setup — the PBX has no way to distinguish this from a regular phone extension except by naming convention. See the Grandstream/Cisco ATA fax-provisioning entries for the exact settings that make fax actually work over one of these.

title: DID (Direct Inward Dial)
body: A DID is a phone number routed directly to an Extension (as opposed to a Ring Group, IVR, or other destination). Configured via FreePBX's Inbound Routes module.

title: Time Conditions / Time Groups
body: Time Conditions control call routing based on a Time Group or Calendar (open/closed hours). Time Groups define the actual periods of time, selected within Time Conditions or Outbound Routes.

title: Extension
body: An Extension is a 3+ digit identifier an endpoint uses to communicate with FreePBX. Can be assigned to physical phones, softphones, ATAs, paging devices (Algo), or virtual voicemail. From a Hosted billing standpoint, any such provisioned entity is a "Hosted Seat."

title: Attended vs Blind Transfer
body: Attended Transfer: the transferring agent stays on the line to speak with the receiving agent before completing the transfer. Blind/Unattended Transfer: the call is transferred without speaking to the receiving party first.

title: Hold vs Park
body: Hold only holds the call on that specific phone — it must be transferred or Parked for another extension to pick it up. Park Lines are BLF buttons for quickly parking a call and picking it up from any phone by dialing the parking lot number or pressing the same Park Line button.

title: DND (Do Not Disturb)
body: DND puts an extension in an Unavailable state, forcing calls to the extension's Unavailable destination. The endpoint does not ring while DND is enabled.

title: Network recommendations for hosted PBX phones
body: Open all ports TO/FROM the PBX IP (phones register on 5060 then get reassigned a random port). Increase UDP timeout to 90s+ — lower values risk registration drops. Avoid double-NAT. Disable SIP ALG — known to cause issues. DHCP Options: Time Offset (opt 2, hex), Time Server (opt 42), Provisioning server (opt 66/160, http://provisioner.123.net). Provisioning server ICMP is disabled by design — don't rely on ping to check it.

title: Ports to open for Hosted PBX
body: UDP/TCP 5060-5061 (SIP signaling). UDP 10000-32767 (RTP media, provider-side range may vary — check current provider docs before assuming a fixed range on new deployments).

title: Monitor a Ring Group via BLF
body:
In extensions_custom.conf, add a hint line mapping the ring group number to its member channels, e.g.:
  exten=>1001,hint,PJSIP/2001&PJSIP/2002&PJSIP/2003
(replace 1001 with the actual ring group number and PJSIP/xxxx with its member extensions). Then on each phone add a BLF resource list key pointing at that ring group number — consult the phone's provisioning template for the exact attendant.resourcelist.* / linekey.* syntax for that model.

title: Email notification on missed call
body:
In extensions_custom.conf, a TrySystem() step can shell out to `mail` on a missed-call leg to notify an address, before falling through to voicemail, e.g.:
  exten => 101,1,TrySystem(echo "Missed Call - From: ${CALLERID(name)} ${CALLERID(number)} received at ${STRFTIME(${EPOCH},,%l:%M:%S %p %Z on %A %B %e)}" | mail -s "PBX Alert - Missed Call" -r "PBX Alerts<FROM_ADDRESS>" TO_ADDRESS)
  exten => 101,n,Goto(ext-local,vmu101,1)
Note: this disables the busy greeting if applicable, and the extension will get two emails if Voicemail-to-Email is also enabled on it. Replace FROM_ADDRESS/TO_ADDRESS with real addresses — never commit real customer email addresses into shared dialplan snippets.

title: Live call monitoring / listen-in (ChanSpy)
body: Dial 555 from any internal phone, authenticate with that PBX's monitor PIN (site-specific — check /etc/asterisk/monitor_pin.conf on that box, don't assume a shared default), then enter the target extension to listen in on. Press 9 to enter a new extension at any time, or * for the next available call. Mute yourself on the spy channel if you don't want the monitored party to hear you.

title: Server and module updates
body: `yum update` for OS/package updates. `fwconsole ma upgradeall` for FreePBX module updates.

title: Repair permissions / "Tampered File" error
body: `fwconsole ma refreshsignatures` re-signs/repairs module files when FreePBX reports a tampered-file error.

title: FreePBX-to-VPBX extension sync (billing/device tracking)
body: A provisioner cron job on the internal provisioning host periodically pulls extension/device data from customer PBXs (via a scoped read-only MySQL grant on that PBX's `asterisk` database) to keep the VPBX billing/device-tracking page in sync. Setting this up on a new PBX requires an internal provisioning-host config change plus a GRANT SELECT on that PBX's asterisk DB for the provisioner's source IP — this is an internal 123.Net process, not something freepbx-tools automates; credentials for it must never be hardcoded anywhere.

title: "Comedian Mail" voicemail prompt
body: "Comedian Mail" is a historical Asterisk/FreePBX voicemail prompt name, inherited from an early open-source voicemail system called "Comedian Mailbox." It's just tradition/leftover branding — the prompts/recordings can be fully customized per-system if a customer wants different wording.

title: N11 short codes (211-911) and extension conflicts
body: The FCC reserves N11 short codes (e.g. 211 for social services, 911 for emergency) for specific services. An internal extension can't reuse one of these numbers — dialing or transferring to it would just reach the public N11 service instead of the internal destination.

title: Feature Codes: Blacklist
body: *30 Blacklist a number. *32 Blacklist the last caller. *31 Remove a number from the blacklist.

title: Feature Codes: Call Forward
body: *72 Activate Call Forward All. *73 Deactivate Call Forward All. *93 Activate Call Forward All (prompting). *74 Deactivate Call Forward All (prompting). *90 Activate Call Forward Busy. *91 Deactivate Call Forward Busy. *94 Activate Call Forward Busy (prompting). *92 Deactivate Call Forward Busy (prompting). *52 Activate Call Forward No Answer/Unavailable. *53 Deactivate Call Forward No Answer/Unavailable. *95 Activate Call Forward No Answer/Unavailable (prompting). *96 Toggle Call Forward.

title: Feature Codes: Call Waiting, Conferences, Contact Manager
body: Call Waiting: *70 activate, *71 deactivate. Conferences: *87 conference status. Contact Manager: *10 speed dials.

title: Feature Codes: Core (pickup, transfer, recording, ChanSpy)
body: *8 General call pickup. 555 ChanSpy. ** Directed call pickup / in-call disconnect. *2 In-call attended transfer. ## In-call blind transfer. *1 Toggle call recording (in-call). 7777 Simulate an incoming call.

title: Feature Codes: Dictation and Do Not Disturb
body: Dictation: *34 perform dictation, *35 email completed dictation. DND: *78 activate, *79 deactivate, *76 toggle.

title: Feature Codes: Fax, Find Me/Follow, Wake Up Calls
body: 666 Dial the System FAX extension. *21 Toggle Find Me/Follow. *68 Set a wake-up call (hotel/PMS use).

title: Feature Codes: Info Services
body: *69 Call trace. *43 Echo test. *65 Speak your extension number. *60 Speaking clock.

title: Feature Codes: Paging and Parking
body: Paging: *80 intercom prefix, *54 allow user intercom, *55 disallow user intercom. Parking: *88 park to your assigned lot, *85 pickup-parked-call prefix, *86 force park into a private lot (Parking Pro).

title: Feature Codes: Queues, Directory, Speed Dial, Voicemail
body: Queues: *45 dynamic-member login/logout toggle, *47 playback queue caller count, *46 queue pause toggle. Directory: 411 dial-by-name. Speed Dial: *75 set user speed dial, *0 speed dial prefix. Voicemail: *98 dial voicemail, * direct dial prefix, *97 my voicemail.

title: Create a standard PJSIP extension
body: Applications > Extensions > Quick Create Extension. Enter extension number, name, outbound caller ID (org support-line CID for internal support extensions), email address. Next. Set Voicemail PIN to 123+extension#. Finish. Then edit the new extension: Voicemail tab -> Email Attachment = Yes. Advanced tab -> Max Contacts = 10, Account Code = the extension number. Submit, then click Apply Config.

title: Create a Let's Encrypt certificate on a customer PBX
body: Admin > Certificate Management > +New Certificate > Generate Let's Encrypt Certificate. Owner's Email: hosted@123.net (org standard). Country: United States. State: Michigan. Check "Remove DST Root CA X3", then Generate Certificate. Then Admin > System Admin > HTTPS Setup > Settings tab: pick the new cert under Certificate Manager, Import, then Save and Restart Apache. Port Management: force Admin port 80 -> 443, Update Now. Connectivity > Firewall > Services: Web Management = Local only, Web Management (Secure) = Internet and Local. Apply Config.

title: Configure alternate ringtones on Yealink phones
body: Yealinks have built-in tone files Ring1.wav-Ring13.wav (viewable on-phone under Sounds, or web GUI under Settings > Preference). To assign a specific ringtone to a Ring Group, Queue, or Inbound Route: on the FreePBX side, find that function's "Alert Info" field, choose Custom, and enter "ringtone-RingN.wav" (case-sensitive, e.g. "ringtone-Ring3.wav" for Ring3.wav). For a fully custom sound, export as WAV/8000Hz (Audacity works), upload it to the phone itself via its web GUI (it must be stored locally on the device, filename case-sensitive), then reference that filename the same way in Alert Info.

title: Grandstream HT802 ATA provisioning (incl. fax pass-through)
body:
Standard 123.Net Grandstream HT802 ATA provisioning steps:
1. On first login, change the admin password (standard fleet default: 08520852123Net) via System Settings > Security Settings > User Info Management.
2. Disable auto-provisioning: Maintenance > Upgrade — uncheck "Allow DHCP Option 43/66/100 to Override Server" and "Auto Provision", set Automatic Upgrade = No, Firmware Upgrade/Provisioning = Always Skip the Firmware Check.
3. Disable TR-069: System Settings > Management Settings — uncheck Enable TR-069.
4. Time zone: System Settings > Time and Language — GMT-05:00 (Eastern).
5. DHCP hostname: Network Settings > Ethernet Settings > General Settings — Host Name (Option 12) = CustomerHandle_ATA.
6. Per FXS port (Port Settings > FXS Port): set Primary SIP Server to the PBX IP, SIP User ID / Authenticate ID to the extension number, Authenticate Password to that extension's secret. Under Call Settings, disable Call Waiting / Call Waiting Caller ID / Call Waiting Tone, set Ring Timeout = 90. Under Codec Settings: all vocoder choices (1-8) = PCMU, Fax Mode = Pass Through, Re-Invite After Fax Tone Detected = Enabled, Jitter Buffer Type = Adaptive, Jitter Buffer Length = High. Under Analog Signal Line Configuration: TX gain -6dB, RX default, Line Echo Canceller (LEC) disabled. Under Call Feature Settings: Enable Local/Call Features = No.
FAX MODE + RE-INVITE ON FAX TONE are the two settings that most directly affect whether a physical fax machine behind this ATA actually completes faxes — check these first when troubleshooting a fax DID that resolves to a Grandstream ATA.

title: Phones boot-looping on a Cisco Catalyst 3550 PoE switch
body:
Known issue: a Cisco Catalyst 3550 PoE switch can cause phones (Polycom VVX and others) to boot-loop instead of powering up cleanly. Fix: on the interfaces the phones are connected to, run:
  power inline delay shutdown 20 initial 300
Reference: Digium/Sangoma support article on Catalyst 3550 PoE causing phones not to boot correctly.

title: Cisco SPA122 ATA provisioning (incl. fax pass-through)
body:
Standard 123.Net Cisco SPA122 ATA provisioning steps:
1. Factory reset via the physical Reset button.
2. Log in locally (default admin/admin) via the ATA's Ethernet port at 192.168.15.1 (Web Access is disabled by default until configured). Administration > Firmware Upgrade first.
3. Administration > User List — edit admin user, set password to the standard fleet default (08520852), submit.
4. Administration > Web Access Management — enable Remote Management.
5. Network Setup > Internet Settings — Host Name = CustomerHandle + ATA (or similar identifier).
6. Network Setup > Time Settings — Eastern time zone.
7. Voice > Provisioning — set Provisioning Enable = No.
8. Voice > Line 1: Network Settings — Jitter Buffer Adjustment = No, Network Jitter Level = Very High. Proxy and Registration — PBX IP. Subscriber Information — extension number in Display Name/User ID/Auth ID. Supplementary Service Subscription — Call Waiting/Three Way Conf/Service Announcement Serv = No. Audio Configuration — Second Preferred Codec = G711a; set G729a Enable, G726a Enable, FAX V21 Detect Enable, FAX CNG Detect Enable, FAX Codec Symmetric, FAX Process NSE, FAX Disable ECAN, FAX T38 ECM Enable, Modem Line, Use Pref Codec Only, FAX Enable T38 all = Yes; FAX Passthru Method = ReINVITE; Echo Canc Enable = No; FAX Tone Detect Mode = Caller or Callee.
The FAX T38/passthru and FAX tone-detect settings are the ones to check first when a fax DID resolving to a Cisco SPA122 isn't completing faxes reliably.

title: Polycom common config fixes (NTP, DND, URL dialing, hold ringback, hard reprovision)
body:
NTP/date-time: override via device.sntp.gmtoffsetcityid / device.sntp.servername (north-america.pool.ntp.org) and tcpipapp.sntp.* attributes in the phone/site config; org standard NTP target is Google's 216.239.35.12 rather than an internal PBX IP.
Remove DND lockout: set feature.doNotDisturb.enable = 0.
Unexpected "URL dialing" behavior on incoming calls (address shown as sip:number@ip instead of caller ID): set feature.urlDialing.enabled = 0 in Global Config.
Enable hold ringback (reminder tone while a call is on hold): add <holdReminder call.hold.localReminder.enabled="1"/> to the site/phone config above the closing </polycomConfig> tag.
Hard reprovision from the phone itself: Home > Settings > Advanced (password 08520852, fallback 456) > Administration Settings > Network Configuration > Provisioning Server — set Boot Server = Static, Server Type = HTTP, Server Address = provisioner.123.net. Then in Network Configuration > DNS Server, set 8.8.8.8. Let the phone reboot/reprovision fully (may reboot more than once).

title: Polycom D230 wireless phone provisioning (discontinued — replace with Yealink W60/56H)
body: D230 was discontinued in 2022 — any D230 having issues should be replaced with a Yealink W60/56H rather than repaired, per org policy. If provisioning one anyway: it's a standalone extension, no VVX sync needed, PoE or external power. Must be manually added to the VPBX page (template, MAC, name, extension, secret) for billing/tracking — no working auto-provisioning template exists for this model. Firmware must be 7.1.1+. Basestation web UI default login is admin/admin, then set a new password on first login. Key config: WAN Settings time service = Eastern; Auto Provisioning server URL = provisioner.123.net; ITSP Profile A digit map and SIP proxy/registrar = the target PBX IP; X_CallParkMethod = REFER, X_DirectedCallPickupMethod = INVITE+Replaces, X_CallParkStatusMethod = Dialog/BLF; feature codes Directed Pickup=**, Pickup=*8, Park=*88; SP1 AuthUserName/AuthPassword = the extension number/secret; voicemail check code = *97; Call Park Extensions = 71-79; disable the OBiTALK service; DECT Wireless basename/handset name = extension. Troubleshooting: reset config via System Management > Device Update > Reset Configuration (basestation) or Settings > Factory Reset (handset); swap power supply/battery/basestation/handset individually to isolate a hardware fault.

title: Polycom park line (BLF) attribute indexes by VVX model
body: Park lines are configured as attendant.resourcelist.N BLF entries (address=parking-lot-ext@pbx-ip, calladdress=*85 + lot-ext@pbx-ip, type=automata) paired with a matching linekey.N.category=BLF/linekey.N.index=N — but the starting index N differs by model since lower indexes are used by the phone's own line keys first: VVX400 park lines typically start at index 7, VVX500 at index 9, VVX600 at index 13. Always confirm against that specific phone's existing linekey usage before assuming the model-default starting index, since a phone with extra provisioned features may already occupy some of those slots.

title: Polycom Enhanced Feature Key (EFK) linekey with user prompt
body: To build a phone button that dials a feature code plus a user-entered value (e.g. an Intercom button that prompts for a target extension), enable feature.enhancedFeatureKeys.enabled=1 and feature.EFKLineKey.enabled=1, then define an efk.efklist.X entry (mname/label = button text, action.string = the feature code with a $PxN4$ placeholder for the prompted digits, e.g. *80$P2N4$$Tinvite$ for Intercom) plus a matching efk.efkprompt.Y (label = prompt text, type=numeric), and bind it with linekey.LINENUM.category=EFK / linekey.LINENUM.index=X. The Intercom example: efk.efklist.2 action.string=*80$P2N4$$Tinvite$, efkprompt.2 label=Extension, linekey.2 category=EFK index=2.

title: Yealink standard provisioning template (non-EOL models)
body: Standard 123.Net Yealink config for current (non-EOL) models T46U/T48U/T54W/T57W: static DNS 8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4, MWI subscribed, caller-ID source from network, remote phonebook enabled (1hr refresh), NTP via pool.ntp.org with Eastern time zone (-5, DST auto), voicemail number = *97, auto-provision server = http://provisioner.123.net/ (protected from override), admin password set to the standard fleet default (08520852). Programmable key 2 defaults to Directory. Useful as a comparison baseline when a Yealink's behavior (wrong time, no MWI, phonebook not loading, not reprovisioning) doesn't match what a freshly-provisioned phone should look like.

title: MikroTik standard on-net Hosted router template
body: Standard 123.Net MikroTik template for an on-net Hosted install: separate VLANs for uplink/management (102) and phones (202, its own DHCP pool e.g. 172.16.123.10-250). DHCP option set for phones includes GMT offset (opt 2), NTP (opt 42), and dual provisioning-server options (opt 66 and opt 160, both http://provisioner.123.net) plus a phone-VLAN option (opt 128). Firewall allow-lists 123.Net's own PBX/provisioning network ranges plus the local management and phone VLANs, drops everything else inbound except established/related; NATs the phone VLAN out; disables unused exposed services (ftp/tftp/h323/sip/pptp) on the router itself. System clock set to America/Detroit with NTP client enabled against 123.Net's NTP servers. Useful as a reference when a customer's on-net router config looks non-standard and phones aren't provisioning/registering correctly — compare against this template's VLAN/DHCP-option/firewall structure rather than guessing.
